_comment: Hand-authored demo corpus. The owner is a solo consultant juggling six clients. These threads are written to exercise every ledger state and every extractor failure mode on purpose: conditionals, requests, pleasantries, and already-done statements sit next to real commitments so the demo shows discrimination, not just detection. Filler threads are generated on top of this by scripts/build-corpus.mts.

owner.name: Sam Okafor
owner.role: independent operations consultant, six active clients

threads.subject: Vendor shortlist for the Q4 RFP
threads.beat: THE MONEY SHOT. Marcus promises the full vendor list by Sept 12. Sept 23 arrives with nothing. Then a partial list lands, and the row must move to partially_satisfied with the two missing items named.

messages.body:
Marcus,

Good session this morning. To keep the RFP on track I need the full vendor list from your side so I can start scoring against the rubric.

I'll have the scoring rubric itself over to you by Wednesday.

Sam

Sam,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. I'll get you the full vendor list by end of day Friday so you can start scoring them.

Happy to loop in Priya on the procurement side if that's useful. Let's maybe sync sometime next month about the renewal too.

Marcus

Perfect. Attached is the scoring rubric as promised.

Sam

Sam - apologies for the delay here. Sending over what I have so far: eleven of the thirteen vendors, attached.

Still chasing Delacroix Freight and Halvorsen Group, their paperwork is stuck with our legal team. I will get you those two by Thursday.

Marcus

threads.subject: Re: Staffing model draft
threads.beat: Dana renegotiates a date rather than slipping it. The original row must move to renegotiated, not abandoned, and the new date must come from the second message.

messages.body:
Sam,

I'll send you the staffing model draft by the 15th so you can fold it into the ops review.

Dana

Sam - the board moved our budget meeting, which changes the headcount assumptions in the model.

Rather than send you something I'll immediately revise, can we push the staffing model to the 29th? I'd rather give you one good version than two drafts.

Dana

Works for me. The 29th still lands before the ops review.

Sam

threads.subject: Integration spec
threads.beat: Tomas promises, then goes silent for six weeks. Row stays open and overdue - the ledger should NOT guess abandonment without evidence. This is the row the chase draft targets.

messages.body:
Sam,

I'll put together the integration spec for the warehouse endpoints and get it to you next week. Should be straightforward.

Tomas

Tomas - checking in on the integration spec. Anything I can do to unblock it?

Sam

threads.subject: Diligence summary
threads.beat: Ana asks for a summary, then supersedes her own ask before Sam delivers. The first row must go to superseded, NOT satisfied - this is the distinction Nano conflates and Super gets right.

messages.body:
Sam,

Could you pull together a diligence summary on the Mercer deal? Two pages is plenty.

Ana

Will do - I'll have the diligence summary to you Friday.

Sam

Sam, hold off on the diligence summary. The committee pushed Mercer to the November cycle, so it's not needed now.

What I do need instead is the comparables table, by the 25th if you can manage it.

Ana

Understood, shelving the summary. I'll get you the comparables table by the 25th.

Sam

threads.subject: Cold chain audit dates
threads.beat: Clean satisfaction. Kwame promises, Kwame delivers, row closes. The ledger needs at least one uneventful success or the demo looks like it only finds problems.

messages.body:
Sam,

I'll confirm the cold chain audit dates with our three sites and send them across by Tuesday.

Kwame

Dates confirmed, all three sites:

Riverton - Oct 6
Eastgate - Oct 8
Caldwell - Oct 13

Kwame

threads.subject: Process map for the intake team
threads.beat: Sam is the one who is late. The ledger has to be uncomfortable in both directions or it is just a tool for blaming other people.

messages.body:
Sam, when you have a moment - any chance you could share the process map for the intake team? Our new hires start the 21st.

Priya

Of course. I'll have the process map over to you by the 12th, well ahead of the new starters.

Sam

threads.subject: Re: Quarterly check-in
threads.beat: Pure adversarial noise. Every sentence here is a near-commitment that must NOT produce a ledger row: conditional offers, requests, pleasantries, and an already-done statement.

messages.body:
Sam,

Great to catch up yesterday. A few follow-ups:

Happy to introduce you to our Rotterdam team if that would be useful.

Attached is the org chart you asked about.

Could you send over your availability for October? No rush.

We should probably revisit the SLA language at some point.

Let's maybe grab lunch when you're next in the city.

Priya

Thanks Priya, all noted. The org chart is helpful.

If the Rotterdam intro makes sense after the RFP closes I'll take you up on it.

Sam

threads.subject: Re: Invoice discrepancy
threads.beat: A deliberately vague but genuine promise. 'I'll look into it and get back to you' IS a commitment - the extractor must not require a crisp deliverable.

messages.body:
Kwame - the August invoice shows two site visits that I don't have in my records. Could you check?

Sam

Odd. I'll look into it with our finance team and get back to you.

Kwame
